topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Overview of Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning objectives, and sets out the framework for understanding cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and Epigenetic Drivers of Clonal Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how genetic driver mutations and transient epigenetic alterations confer selective growth advantages to clones during tumor evolution.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tissue differentiation hierarchies, stemness properties, and specific cells of origin determine tumor initiation and propagation across leukemias and solid cancers.

topics.label: Role of Microenvironment, Stroma, and Inflammation in Tumor Outgrowth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate that cancer development and established tumor maintenance require permissive microenvironmental signals, inflammatory promoters, and supportive stroma.

topics.label: Advanced Methodologies for Investigating Tumor Heterogeneity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details modern laboratory and computational tools, such as single-cell sequencing and spatial omics, used to map tumor evolution and microenvironmental interactions.

topics.label: Integrated Multi-Factor Model of Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the intersecting roles of mutational burden, cell-of-origin properties, epigenetic plasticity, and microenvironmental coevolution in driving cancer progression.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Preview of Next Session
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the concluding remarks for the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
